question: Under paragraph 1 of the Direction, what name shall these Directions be called?
options: Reserve Bank of India (KYC) Directions, 2016
Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Directions, 2016
Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer (KYC)) Directions, 2016
Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer (KYC)) Directions, 2015 and subsequent amendments
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 1(a)
source_excerpt: (a) These Directions shall be called the Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer (KYC)) Directions, 2016.

question: To whom do the provisions of these Directions primarily apply, as stated in paragraph 2?
options: Every banking company incorporated in India and licensed under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to carry on the business of banking
Every entity regulated by Reserve Bank of India, more specifically as defined in paragraph 3(b)(xiv)
Every financial intermediary registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India
Every branch of a foreign bank located outside India, irrespective of the local laws
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 2(a)
source_excerpt: provisions of these Directions shall apply to every entity regulated by Reserve Bank of India, more specifically as defined in 3 (b) (xiv) below, except where specifically mentioned otherwise.

question: According to the definition of Beneficial Owner, when the customer is a company, who is the beneficial owner?
options: The natural person holding more than 50 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company acting alone or together
The relevant natural person who holds the position of senior managing official of the company where no natural person is identified
The natural person holding more than 25 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company
The natural person(s) who has/have a controlling ownership interest or who exercise control through other means
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(iv)a
source_excerpt: Where the customer is a company , the beneficial owner is the natural person(s), who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or more juridical persons, has/have a controlling ownership interest or who exercise control through other means.

question: Under the Beneficial Owner definition, for an unincorporated association or body of individuals, what share identifies the beneficial owner?
options: More than 10 percent of the property or capital or profits
More than 15 percent of the property or capital or profits
More than 25 percent of the property or capital or profits
More than 50 percent of the property or capital or profits
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(iv)c
source_excerpt: the beneficial owner is the natural person(s), who, whether acting alone or together, or through one or more juridical person, has/have ownership of/entitlement to more than 15 percent of the property or capital or profits of the unincorporated association or body of individuals.

question: What does the Direction mean by Digital KYC?
options: Capturing a live photo of the customer along with the fingerprint impression of the authorised officer
Capturing live photo of the customer and officially valid document or Aadhaar proof, with the latitude and longitude of where such photo is taken
Capturing a live video of the customer signing the account opening form
Capturing a live photo of the customer with a scanned copy of the PAN sent by email
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(viii)
source_excerpt: means the capturing live photo of the customer and officially valid document or the proof of possession of Aadhaar, where offline verification cannot be carried out, along with the latitude and longitude of the location where such live photo is being taken by an authorised officer of the RE

question: Which of the following does the Direction list as an Officially Valid Document?
options: A card issued by the Food and Civil Supplies Department of the State Government
A passbook of a scheduled commercial bank showing the customer's address
A job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government
A certificate of net worth issued by a chartered accountant on the customer's behalf
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(xiv)
source_excerpt: proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government and letter issued by the National Population Register containing details of name and address.

question: How does the Direction define the Central KYC Records Registry?
options: A committee constituted by scheduled commercial banks to coordinate and standardise the KYC and customer identification practices across the Indian banking system
An entity defined under Rule 2(1) of the Rules, to receive, store, safeguard and retrieve the KYC records in digital form of a customer
A department of the Reserve Bank of India that verifies KYC documents submitted by regulated entities
An entity established under the Information Technology Act, 2000 that hosts digital lockers of customers
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(vi)
source_excerpt: means an entity defined under Rule 2(1) of the Rules, to receive, store, safeguard and retrieve the KYC records in digital form of a customer.

question: According to the definition in the Direction, who is the Principal Officer?
options: A person designated by the RE to ensure overall compliance with the obligations imposed under chapter IV of the PML Act and the Rules
An officer of the Financial Intelligence Unit - India nominated to receive suspicious transaction reports from regulated entities
An officer at the management level nominated by the RE, responsible for furnishing information as per rule 8 of the Rules
A whole-time director of the Board of the RE nominated to oversee the KYC audit functions
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(xviii)
source_excerpt: means an officer at the management level nominated by the RE, responsible for furnishing information as per rule 8 of the Rules.

question: How is the term customer defined in the Direction?
options: Any person who holds a savings account or a current account with a regulated entity
A person who has an account-based relationship with a regulated entity and operates it
Only a walk-in person who undertakes transactions without any account-based relationship
A person who is engaged in a financial transaction or activity with a Regulated Entity (RE) and includes a person on whose behalf the person who is engaged in the transaction or activity, is acting
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(b)(iii)
source_excerpt: means a person who is engaged in a financial transaction or activity with a Regulated Entity (RE) and includes a person on whose behalf the person who is engaged in the transaction or activity, is acting.

question: What does Customer Due Diligence mean under the Direction?
options: Periodic updation of the documents collected at the time of opening an account
Continuous monitoring of transactions to ensure they are consistent with the customer's risk profile
Identifying and verifying the customer and the beneficial owner using reliable and independent sources of identification
Verifying the identity of a customer only when a suspicious transaction report is filed
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(b)(v)
source_excerpt: means identifying and verifying the customer and the beneficial owner using reliable and independent sources of identification.

question: How does the Direction treat video based customer identification processes that comply with the prescribed standards and procedures?
options: As an inferior alternative that requires additional documentary evidence from the customer
On par with face-to-face CIP for the purpose of this Master Direction
As applicable only to non-face-to-face customers opening accounts through digital channels
On par with digital KYC, requiring recording of the latitude and longitude of the location
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(b)(xvi)
source_excerpt: shall be treated on par with face- to-face CIP for the purpose of this Master Direction.

question: Which of the following is included within the meaning of Regulated Entities under paragraph 3(b)(xiv)?
options: Companies registered under section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 for charitable purposes
Entities that are regulated exclusively by the Securities and Exchange Board of India
All Payment System Providers (PSPs)/ System Participants (SPs) and Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuers (PPI Issuers)
Non-profit organisations registered as trusts or societies under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(b)(xiv)
source_excerpt: All Payment System Providers (PSPs)/ System Participants (SPs) and Prepaid Payment Instrument Issuers (PPI Issuers) f. All authorised persons (APs) including those who are agents of Money Transfer Service Scheme (MTSS), regulated by the Regulator.

question: According to the definition in the Direction, what is a shell bank?
options: A bank that operates only through mobile applications without any brick-and-mortar branches in India
A bank incorporated in a tax haven whose Indian subsidiary does not maintain effective consolidated supervision
A bank that has physical presence in the country of incorporation but is unaffiliated with any regulated financial group

A bank that has no physical presence in the country in which it is incorporated and licensed, and which is unaffiliated with a regulated financial group that is subject to effective consolidated supervision
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(b)(xv)
source_excerpt: means a bank that has no physical presence in the country in which it is incorporated and licensed, and which is unaffiliated with a regulated financial group that is subject to effective consolidated supervision.

question: Who must approve the Know Your Customer policy of a regulated entity?
options: The Board of Directors of REs or any committee of the Board to which power has been delegated
The Designated Director in consultation with the Principal Officer of the entity
The Reserve Bank of India before the policy is implemented by the entity
The Financial Intelligence Unit - India through its registration portal
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 4(a)
source_excerpt: There shall be a Know Your Customer (KYC) policy duly approved by the Board of Directors of REs or any committee of the Board to which power has been delegated.

question: Which set of four key elements must the KYC policy include?
options: Customer Acceptance Policy; Risk Management; Customer Identification Procedures (CIP); and Monitoring of Transactions
Customer Acceptance Policy; Risk Management; Employee Screening; and Staff Training
Customer Identification Procedures (CIP); Enhanced Due Diligence; Record Keeping; and Reporting
Risk Management; Transaction Reporting; Audit; and Correspondent Banking Controls
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 5
source_excerpt: The KYC policy shall include following four key elements: (a) Customer Acceptance Policy; (b) Risk Management; (c) Customer Identification Procedures (CIP); and (d) Monitoring of Transactions

question: How often should the ML/TF risk assessment exercise be reviewed, according to paragraph 5A?
options: At least once every three years, as determined by the Board of the RE
It should be reviewed at least annually
Quarterly, based on the outcome of transaction monitoring
Half-yearly, in line with the guidance issued by the FATF
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 5A(b)
source_excerpt: the periodicity of risk assessment exercise shall be determined by the Board or any committee of the Board of the RE to which power in this regard has been delegated, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, it should be reviewed at least annually.

question: Which of the following is specified as a means of ensuring compliance with the KYC policy?
options: Submission of quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee
Submission of half-yearly compliance reports directly to the Reserve Bank of India
Filing of annual KYC compliance statements with the Financial Intelligence Unit - India
Constitution of a KYC committee of customers for independent evaluation of policies
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 8(a)(v)
source_excerpt: Concurrent/internal audit system to verify the compliance with KYC/AML policies and procedures. (v) Submission of quarterly audit notes and compliance to the Audit Committee.

question: What restriction does the Direction place on outsourcing related to KYC compliance?
options: Decision-making functions of determining compliance with KYC norms are not outsourced
Verification of official valid documents cannot be outsourced to business correspondents
CDD data entry functions cannot be outsourced even to group companies of the RE
Periodic updation of KYC records cannot be outsourced to any third party vendor
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 8(b)
source_excerpt: REs shall ensure that decision- making functions of determining compliance with KYC norms are not outsourced.

question: What does the Customer Acceptance Policy ensure regarding the opening of accounts?
options: No account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/benami name
No account is opened for a customer without a permanent address proof
No account is opened without an introduction from an existing account holder
No account is opened for a customer who does not furnish PAN at the time of opening
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 10(a)
source_excerpt: No account is opened in anonymous or fictitious/benami name.

question: Under the Customer Acceptance Policy, what follows from applying CDD at the UCIC level?
options: A fresh CDD exercise is required every time a KYC compliant customer approaches the RE for any product

If an existing KYC compliant customer of a RE desires to open another account or avail any other product or service from the same RE, there shall be no need for a fresh CDD exercise as far as identification of the customer is concerned
A fresh CDD exercise is required only when the customer requests a product with a credit limit above rupees one lakh
CDD at the UCIC level applies only to walk-in customers who do not maintain any account with the RE
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 10(f)
source_excerpt: REs shall apply the CDD procedure at the UCIC level. Thus, if an existing KYC compliant customer of a RE desires to open another account or avail any other product or service from the same RE, there shall be no need for a fresh CDD exercise as far as identification of the customer is concerned.

question: When a Permanent Account Number is obtained, what does the Customer Acceptance Policy require?
options: The PAN shall be verified through the database of the National Securities Depository Limited
The PAN shall be verified by the Designated Director before the account is activated
The same shall be verified from the verification facility of the issuing authority
The PAN shall be verified through a self-declaration signed by the customer
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 10(j)
source_excerpt: Where Permanent Account Number (PAN) is obtained, the same shall be verified from the verification facility of the issuing authority.

question: What requirement does paragraph 11 impose regarding rejection of onboarding or periodic updation applications?
options: Rejections shall be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit - India within fifteen days
No application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC shall be rejected without application of mind, and reason(s) of rejection shall be duly recorded by the officer concerned
Every rejection shall be approved by the Board of Directors of the regulated entity
Rejections shall be communicated in writing to the customer along with an appeal mechanism
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 11
source_excerpt: No application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC shall be rejected without application of mind. Reason(s) of rejection shall be duly recorded by the officer concerned.

question: According to paragraph 11A, what shall an RE do if it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing and believes CDD will tip-off the customer?
options: It shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND
It shall complete the CDD process and file an STR only after the relationship is closed
It shall refer the matter to the Designated Director before deciding on further CDD action
It shall continue CDD but suspend all transactions in the account for ninety days
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 11A
source_excerpt: Where RE forms a suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and it reasonably believes that performing the CDD process will tip-off the customer, it shall not pursue the CDD process, and instead file an STR with FIU-IND.

question: Into which categories does paragraph 12 require customers to be categorised?
options: Low, medium and high-risk category, based on the assessment and risk perception of the RE
Low, medium, high and very high risk categories based on the asset size and deposit balance of the customer
Standard, medium and high risk, based on the type of account operated by the customer
Low, moderate and severe risk, based on the transaction volume of the customer
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 12(a)
source_excerpt: Customers shall be categorised as low, medium and high-risk category, based on the assessment and risk perception of the RE.

question: How does paragraph 12 treat the risk categorisation of a customer and the reasons for it?
options: It shall be kept confidential and shall not be revealed to the customer to avoid tipping off the customer
It shall be disclosed to the customer at the time of periodic updation of KYC records
It shall be shared with all regulated entities in the same group for group-wide risk assessment
It shall be filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit - India on a half-yearly basis
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 12(d)
source_excerpt: The risk categorisation of a customer and the specific reasons for such categorisation shall be kept confidential and shall not be revealed to the customer to avoid tipping off the customer.

question: According to paragraph 13(g), what must REs ensure about introductions when opening accounts?
options: An introduction from an existing customer is required before any account is opened
Introduction is not to be sought while opening accounts
An introduction is needed only when the customer is categorised as high risk
An introduction by a relative may be accepted in place of an officially valid document
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 13(g)
source_excerpt: REs shall ensure that introduction is not to be sought while opening accounts.

question: Under paragraph 13(e), when must an RE undertake identification for a non-account-based walk-in customer?
options: Whenever any single cash transaction, or several transactions that appear to be connected, is carried out for a non-account-based customer at the branch, whatever the amount involved
Only when the customer asks for an international money transfer
When transactions total more than rupees ten thousand in a financial year
When the amount involved is equal to or exceeds rupees fifty thousand, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be connected
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 13(e)
source_excerpt: Carrying out transactions for a non -account-based customer, that is a walk -in customer, where the amount involved is equal to or exceeds rupees fifty thousand, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be connected.

question: In which situation does paragraph 13(f) require the RE to undertake customer identification on suspicion of structuring?
options: When a customer requests removal of a lien on a fixed deposit
When the RE has reason to doubt the authenticity or adequacy of the customer identification data it has obtained, or when third party products are sold as agents for more than rupees fifty thousand
When a RE has reason to believe that a customer is intentionally structuring a transaction into a series of transactions below the threshold of rupees fifty thousand
When a walk-in customer conducts a single transaction of rupees twenty five thousand
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 13(f)
source_excerpt: When a RE has reason to believe that a customer (account- based or walk-in) is intentionally structuring a transaction into a series of transactions below the threshold of rupees fifty thousand.

question: When an RE relies on customer due diligence carried out by a third party, who bears the ultimate responsibility for CDD and enhanced due diligence?
options: The third party that carried out the due diligence
The Central KYC Records Registry
The regulator of the jurisdiction where the third party is based
The RE
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 14(e)
source_excerpt: The ultimate responsibility for customer due diligence and undertaking enhanced due diligence measures, as applicable, will be with the RE.

question: What must an RE do with the records or information of customer due diligence carried out by a third party under paragraph 14(a)?
options: Obtain them only when the account balance crosses rupees one lakh
Obtain them immediately from the third party or from the Central KYC Records Registry
Obtain them at the time of the next periodic review of the account, and only if the RE's compliance officer specifically approves the request
Obtain them only if the third party confirms in writing every year that its systems are adequate
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 14(a)
source_excerpt: Records or the information of the customer due diligence carried out by the third party is obtained immediately from the third party or from the Central KYC Records Registry.

question: Under paragraph 14(d), where must the third party on whose due diligence an RE relies not be based?
options: In a country or jurisdiction assessed as high risk
In any jurisdiction outside the European Union
In a jurisdiction that is a member of the Financial Action Task Force
In a country where the RE itself has no branches
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 14(d)
source_excerpt: The third party shall not be based in a country or jurisdiction assessed as high risk.

question: Under paragraph 16, where offline verification of the Aadhaar number cannot be carried out, what must the RE obtain from the individual?
options: Only the Aadhaar number, with no further document

The proof of possession of Aadhaar number where offline verification can be carried out, along with the Permanent Account Number or the equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60 as defined in Income-tax Rules, 1962
The KYC Identifier with explicit consent to download records from CKYCR
The proof of possession of Aadhaar number where offline verification cannot be carried out or any OVD or the equivalent e-document thereof containing the details of his identity and address
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 16(ab)
source_excerpt: the proof of possession of Aadhaar number where offline verification cannot be carried out or any OVD or the equivalent e- document thereof containing the details of his identity and address

question: When offline verification cannot be carried out for an OVD or Aadhaar proof under clause (ab), how must the RE verify it under paragraph 16?
options: By carrying out e-KYC authentication using the Aadhaar OTP facility
By obtaining a certified copy and a recent photograph of the customer
By carrying out offline verification of the Aadhaar XML file
Through digital KYC as specified under Annex I
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 16, proviso clause (iv)
source_excerpt: any OVD or proof of possession of Aadhaar number under clause (ab) above where offline verification cannot be carried out, the RE shall carry out verification through digital KYC as specified under Annex I.

question: Under paragraph 16(b), what must an RE obtain from an individual for CDD in addition to the identity and address document?
options: The passport number of the individual, if held
The voter identity card issued by the Election Commission
The driving licence issued by the Regional Transport Authority as proof of the customer's current residential address, where it differs
The Permanent Account Number or the equivalent e-document thereof or Form No. 60 as defined in Income-tax Rules, 1962
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 16(b)
source_excerpt: the Permanent Account Number or the equivalent e- document thereof or Form No. 60 as defined in Income-tax Rules, 1962

question: For accounts opened using Aadhaar OTP based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode, what limit applies to the aggregate balance of all the customer's deposit accounts?
options: Rupees fifty thousand
Rupees two lakh
Rupees one lakh
Rupees sixty thousand
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 17(iii)
source_excerpt: The aggregate balance of all the deposit accounts of the customer shall not exceed rupees one lakh.

question: What restriction does paragraph 17(v) place on borrowal accounts opened using OTP based e-KYC in non-face-to-face mode?
options: Only term loans shall be sanctioned, and the aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year
Only housing loans sanctioned up to an aggregate of rupees one lakh in a financial year are permitted, and working capital facilities are barred
No borrowal accounts of any kind may be opened in this mode
Working capital limits up to rupees two lakh may be sanctioned in a year
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 17(v)
source_excerpt: As regards borrowal accounts, only term loans shall be sanctioned. The aggregate amount of term loans sanctioned shall not exceed rupees sixty thousand in a year.

question: If the CDD procedure for accounts opened using OTP based e-KYC is not completed within a year, what does paragraph 17(vii) require?
options: The account continues with a lower transaction limit until CDD is completed
The account is automatically converted into a small account
Deposit accounts shall be closed immediately, and no further debits shall be allowed in borrowal accounts
The RE may extend the period by a further six months at its discretion after recording the reasons in its books
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 17(vii)
source_excerpt: If the CDD procedure as mentioned above is not completed within a year, in respect of deposit accounts, the same shall be closed immediately. In respect of borrowal accounts no further debits shall be allowed.

question: What must the V-CIP infrastructure or application be capable of preventing under paragraph 18?
options: Connection from IP addresses outside India or from spoofed IP addresses
Connection from any mobile network that is not 5G enabled
Video recording of customers located outside municipal limits
Use of end-to-end encryption between the customer device and the hosting point
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(a)(iii)
source_excerpt: The V -CIP infrastructure / application should be capable of preventing connection from IP addresses outside India or from spoofed IP addresses.

question: According to paragraph 18, what must the video recordings of a V-CIP contain about the customer and the timing?
options: The customer's IP address and the server's time stamp
The live GPS co -ordinates (geo-tagging) of the customer undertaking the V-CIP and date-time stamp
The branch code of the RE, the name of the official performing the V-CIP and the customer's IP address at the time of the call
The latitude and longitude of the RE's head office and the date of onboarding
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(a)(iv)
source_excerpt: The video recordings should contain the live GPS co -ordinates (geo-tagging) of the customer undertaking the V-CIP and date-time stamp.

question: Who should conduct the vulnerability assessment, penetration testing and security audit of the V-CIP infrastructure?
options: Empanelled auditors of Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In)
The cloud service provider that hosts the V-CIP application
Any private firm certified by the International Organization for Standardization
The Unique Identification Authority of India
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(a)(vii)
source_excerpt: Such tests should be conducted by the empanelled auditors of Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).

question: Under paragraph 18(b)(vi), which is not one of the listed ways of obtaining identification information during V-CIP?
options: Submission of a printed copy of the equivalent e-document of an OVD
OTP based Aadhaar e-KYC authentication
Offline Verification of Aadhaar for identification
KYC records downloaded from CKYCR using the KYC identifier provided by the customer
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(b)(vi)
source_excerpt: a) OTP based Aadhaar e-KYC authentication b) Offline Verification of Aadhaar for identification c) KYC records downloaded from CKYCR, in accordance with p aragraph 56, using the KYC identifier provided by the customer d) Equivalent e-document of Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) including documents issued through DigiLocker

question: What does paragraph 18(b)(viii) require the V-CIP official to do about the customer's PAN?
options: Obtain a certified copy of the PAN card within three working days of the video process and upload it to the Central KYC Records Registry along with the complete video recording of the interaction
Verify the PAN only from the records of the Central KYC Records Registry
Capture the image of the PAN card only when an e-PAN is not available
Capture a clear image of the PAN card displayed by the customer, except where e-PAN is provided, and verify PAN details from the issuing authority's database including through DigiLocker
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(b)(viii)
source_excerpt: RE shall capture a clear image of PAN card to be displayed by the customer during the process, except in cases where e-PAN is provided by the customer. The PAN details shall be verified from the database of the issuing authority including through DigiLocker.

question: Under paragraph 18(b)(xii), when may an account opened through V-CIP be made operational?
options: As soon as the authorised official completes the video interaction
Once the customer uploads the equivalent e-document of the PAN to DigiLocker and the RE confirms the digital signature on the document
After the RE receives confirmation of the KYC records downloaded from CKYCR
Only after being subject to concurrent audit, to ensure the integrity of process and its acceptability of the outcome
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(b)(xii)
source_excerpt: All accounts opened through V-CIP shall be made operational only after being subject t o concurrent audit, to ensure the integrity of process and its acceptability of the outcome.

question: Where must the entire data and recordings of V-CIP be stored under paragraph 18(c)?
options: In a system or systems located in India
On the servers of the cloud service provider, wherever located
At the RE's overseas data processing centre
With the third-party technology provider that assists the V-CIP
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 18(c)(i)
source_excerpt: The entire data and recordings of V-CIP shall be stored in a system / systems located in India.

question: What does paragraph 23(i) provide about foreign remittances credited into a small account?
options: Foreign remittances may be credited up to rupees ten thousand per month
Foreign remittances are credited only after the account has remained operational for the initial twelve months and the customer has furnished evidence of having applied for an OVD
Foreign remittance shall not be allowed to be credited into the account unless the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18
Foreign remittances are permitted only at branches linked to Core Banking Solution
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23(i)
source_excerpt: Foreign remittance shall not be allowed to be credited into the account unless the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

question: How long does a small account remain operational initially, and on what condition can it be extended?
options: Six months initially, extendable by a further six months on the customer's request

Twelve months initially, which the bank may extend at its discretion for any further period without requiring the customer to apply for an OVD during the first twelve months of the opening of the account or to furnish any evidence in support
Twelve months initially, extendable for a further twelve months if the holder applies and furnishes evidence of having applied for any of the OVDs during the first twelve months
Twenty-four months initially, with no provision for extension
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23(e)
source_excerpt: The account shall remain operational initially for a period of twelve months which can be extended for a further period of twelve months, provided the account holder applies and furnishes evidence of having applied for any of the OVDs during the first twelve months of the opening of the said account.

question: Which set of transaction and balance limits does paragraph 23 impose on a small account?
options: Aggregate credits up to rupees fifty thousand in a financial year, withdrawals and transfers up to rupees twenty thousand a month, and balance up to rupees twenty thousand at any time
Aggregate credits up to rupees one lakh in a financial year, withdrawals and transfers up to rupees ten thousand a month, and balance up to rupees fifty thousand
Aggregate credits up to rupees two lakh in a financial year, withdrawals and transfers up to rupees five thousand a month, and balance up to rupees twenty-five thousand
Aggregate credits up to rupees one lakh in a financial year, withdrawals and transfers up to rupees twenty thousand a month, and balance up to rupees fifty thousand
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23, clauses (i) to (iii)
source_excerpt: i. the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed rupees one lakh; ii. the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed rupees ten thousand; and iii. the balance at any point of time does not exceed rupees fifty thousand.

question: Under the NBFC simplified procedure in paragraph 24(g), when must the customer be notified to submit appropriate KYC documents?
options: When the balance reaches rupees forty thousand or the total credit in a year reaches rupees eighty thousand

When the balance reaches rupees twenty thousand or the total credit in a year reaches rupees fifty thousand, the customer must submit appropriate KYC documents or operations in the account will be stopped
When the account has been operational for twelve months
When the balance reaches rupees fifty thousand or the total credit in a year reaches rupees one lakh
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 24(g)
source_excerpt: The customer shall be notified when the balance reaches rupees forty thousand or the total credit in a year reaches rupees eighty thousand that appropriate documents for conducting the KYC must be submitted otherwise the operations in the account shall be stopped when the total balance in all the accounts taken together exceeds the limits prescribed in direction (d) and (e) above.

question: What balance and credit limits apply to accounts opened by NBFCs under the simplified procedure in paragraph 24?
options: Balance up to rupees one lakh at any point of time and total credit up to rupees two lakh in a year across all accounts taken together
Balance up to rupees twenty thousand and total credit up to rupees fifty thousand in a year across all accounts

Balances in all their accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees eighty thousand at any point of time, and the total credit in all the accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees one lakh fifty thousand in a year

Balances in all their accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees fifty thousand at any point of time, and the total credit in all the accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees one lakh in a year
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 24, clauses (d) and (e)
source_excerpt: Balances in all their accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees fifty thousand at any point of time. (e) The total credit in all the accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees one lakh in a year.

question: When is a KYC verification done by one branch or office of an RE valid for transferring the account to another branch or office of the same RE?
options: Always, regardless of when the KYC verification was carried out, whether the account is due for periodic updation, or which branch holds the records
Only if the customer signs a fresh application at the receiving branch
Provided full KYC verification has already been done for the concerned account and the same is not due for periodic updation
Only if the receiving branch is located in the same city as the transferring branch
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 26
source_excerpt: KYC verification once done by one branch/office of the RE shall be valid for transfer of the account to any other branch/office of the same RE, provided full KYC verification has already been done for the concerned account and the same is not due for periodic updation.

question: Under the risk management provisions of the Direction, into which categories shall customers be categorised by a regulated entity?
options: As low and high-risk categories only, since medium risk is not recognised by the RE
As low, moderate and high-risk categories based solely on the products and services availed
As moderate and high-risk categories only, because low-risk customers are exempt from assessment
As low, medium and high-risk category, based on the assessment and risk perception of the RE
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 12(a)
source_excerpt: Customers shall be categorised as low, medium and high-risk category, based on the assessment and risk perception of the RE.

question: What does the Direction require an RE to do with the risk categorisation of a customer and the specific reasons for it?
options: Communicate it to the customer in writing whenever the categorisation is carried out
Share it with the customer on request where the customer falls in the low risk category
Keep it confidential and not reveal it to the customer to avoid tipping off the customer
Disclose it to the customer along with the reasons within thirty days of the categorisation
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 12(d)
source_excerpt: The risk categorisation of a customer and the specific reasons for such categorisation shall be kept confidential and shall not be revealed to the customer to avoid tipping off the customer.

question: Which set of transaction limits applies to a small account opened as an alternative under paragraph 23?
options: Credits up to rupees fifty thousand a year, withdrawals up to rupees five thousand a month and balance up to rupees ten thousand
Credits up to rupees two lakh a year, withdrawals up to rupees twenty thousand a month and balance up to rupees one lakh
Credits up to rupees one lakh a year, withdrawals and transfers up to rupees ten thousand a month and balance up to rupees fifty thousand
Credits up to rupees one lakh a year, withdrawals up to rupees ten thousand a month and balance up to rupees one lakh
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23
source_excerpt: i. the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed rupees one lakh; ii. the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed rupees ten thousand; and iii. the balance at any point of time does not exceed rupees fifty thousand.

question: Under paragraph 23, how long does a small account remain operational initially and when are the relaxation provisions reviewed?
options: It remains operational for twelve months only, and the relaxation provisions are reviewed after twelve months
It remains operational for six months, extendable by another six months, and reviewed after twenty-four months
It remains operational initially for twelve months, extendable for a further twelve months, and reviewed after twelve months
It remains operational initially for twelve months, extendable for a further twelve months, and reviewed after twenty-four months
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23(e)
source_excerpt: The account shall remain operational initially for a period of twelve months which can be extended for a further period of twelve months, provided the account holder applies and furnishes evidence of having applied for any of the OVDs during the first twelve months of the opening of the said account. (f) The entire relaxation provisions shall be reviewed after twenty-four months.

question: According to paragraph 23, when may a foreign remittance be credited into a small account?
options: Only when the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18
Whenever the account holder furnishes evidence of having applied for an officially valid document
Whenever the designated officer of the bank certifies the signature of the account holder
Only after the relaxation provisions have been reviewed after twenty-four months
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 23(i)
source_excerpt: Foreign remittance shall not be allowed to be credited into the account unless the identity of the customer is fully established as per paragraph 16 or paragraph 18.

question: Under the simplified procedure of paragraph 24 for NBFCs, what balance and credit ceilings apply to the customer's accounts taken together?
options: Balance up to rupees one lakh at any time and total credit up to rupees two lakh in a year
Balance up to rupees fifty thousand at any time and total credit up to rupees fifty thousand in a year
Balance up to rupees fifty thousand at any time and total credit up to rupees one lakh in a year
Balance up to rupees twenty-five thousand at any time and total credit up to rupees fifty thousand in a year
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 24(d)
source_excerpt: Balances in all their accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees fifty thousand at any point of time. (e) The total credit in all the accounts taken together shall not exceed rupees one lakh in a year.

question: Pending verification of the local address, on what conditions may a foreign student's account be operated during the 30-day period?
options: Foreign remittances not exceeding USD 5,000 or equivalent are allowed with an aggregate cap of rupees one lakh during the 30-day period
No foreign remittance is allowed at all and the aggregate balance is capped at rupees ten thousand
Foreign remittances not exceeding USD 1,000 or equivalent are allowed with an aggregate cap of rupees fifty thousand
Foreign remittances are unrestricted but the aggregate balance is capped at rupees one lakh
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 44(a)
source_excerpt: Provided further that pending the verification of address, the account shall be operated with a condition of allowing foreign remittances not exceeding USD 1,000 or equivalent into the account and a cap of rupees fifty thousand on aggregate in the same, during the 30-day period.

question: If an existing customer fails to submit PAN, its equivalent e-document or Form No. 60 by the date notified by the Central Government, what must the RE do?
options: Temporarily cease operations in the account until the customer submits it
Close the account immediately after settling all obligations due on it
Convert the account into a small account subject to the limits of paragraph 23
Continue normal operations and merely record the non-submission in the RE's records
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 39
source_excerpt: failing which RE shall temporarily cease operations in the account till the time the Permanent Account Number or equivalent e-documents thereof or Form No. 60 is submitted by the customer.

question: Which of these must be obtained as a certified copy or its equivalent e-document for opening an account of a company under paragraph 30?
options: Partnership deed of the company along with the PAN of every partner of the company
Certificate of registration issued by the municipal authorities under the Shop and Establishment Act along with the sales and income tax returns of the firm
A resolution from the Board of Directors and power of attorney granted to its managers, officers or employees to transact on its behalf
Trust deed together with the names of the beneficiaries, trustees, settlor and protector of the trust
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 30
source_excerpt: A resolution from the Board of Directors and power of attorney granted to its managers, officers or employees to transact on its behalf

question: Under paragraph 31, which document must be obtained in addition to the registration certificate and partnership deed for a partnership firm's account?
options: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the partnership firm
Certificate of incorporation of the partnership firm
Permanent Account Number of the partnership firm
A resolution from the Board of Directors of the partnership firm
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 31
source_excerpt: Registration certificate (b) Partnership deed (c) 94Permanent Account Number of the partnership firm

question: Under paragraph 32, which constitutive document must be obtained as a certified copy or equivalent e-document when opening an account of a trust?
options: Trust deed
Memorandum and Articles of Association of the trust
Partnership deed of the trust
Certificate of incorporation of the trust
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 32
source_excerpt: certified copies of each of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof shall be obtained: (a) Registration certificate (b) Trust deed

question: For an account of a juridical person not specifically covered earlier, such as a society, university or local body, what must be obtained under paragraph 33B?
options: Partnership deed of the juridical person along with the PAN of all its partners
Document showing name of the person authorised to act on behalf of the entity
Memorandum and Articles of Association of the entity certified by a notary public
Trust deed of the entity together with the list of its beneficiaries and trustees
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 33B
source_excerpt: Document showing name of the person authorised to act on behalf of the entity (b) Documents, as specified in paragraph 16, of the person holding an attorney to transact on its behalf

question: Under the definition of Beneficial Owner, what counts as a controlling ownership interest in a company?
options: Ownership of or entitlement to at least 25 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company
Ownership of or entitlement to more than 15 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company
Ownership of or entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company
Ownership of or entitlement to 51 percent or more of the voting rights in the company
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(iv)
source_excerpt: Controlling ownership interest means ownership of/entitlement to more than 10 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the company.

question: For a customer that is an unincorporated association or a body of individuals, what ownership level identifies the beneficial owner?
options: More than 10 percent of the property or capital or profits of the association
At least 25 percent of the shares or capital or profits of the association
Any holding of property or capital, however small, in the association
More than 15 percent of the property or capital or profits of the unincorporated association or body of individuals
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(iv)
source_excerpt: has/have ownership of/entitlement to more than 15 percent of the property or capital or profits of the unincorporated association or body of individuals.

question: When the customer is a trust, whose identification does the Direction say must be included in identifying the beneficial owner?
options: The trustees of the trust alone, since the Direction does not require identification of beneficiaries
The author, the trustee and the beneficiaries holding more than 15 percent interest in the trust
The author of the trust, the trustee, the beneficiaries with 10 percent or more interest in the trust and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control
The beneficiaries holding 25 percent or more interest in the trust and the settlor of the trust
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 3(a)(iv)
source_excerpt: the identification of beneficial owner(s) shall include identification of the author of the trust, the trustee, the beneficiaries with 10 percent or more interes t in the trust and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust through a chain of control or ownership.

question: Under the enhanced due diligence measures for non-face-to-face onboarding in paragraph 40, what must the first transaction in such an account be?
options: A cash deposit made at a branch of the RE within thirty days of account opening
A debit to the account towards the account opening charges of the customer
A credit from any bank account of the customer, whether or not it is KYC-complied
A credit from an existing KYC-complied bank account of the customer
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 40(e)
source_excerpt: First transaction in such accounts shall be a credit from existing KYC-complied bank account of the customer.

question: Under paragraph 34, when is it not necessary to identify and verify the identity of any shareholder or beneficial owner?
options: When the customer is a trust and the trustees have disclosed their status at the time of commencement of the account-based relationship
When the customer is a small account holder whose aggregate balance never exceeds rupees fifty thousand at any point of time
When the beneficial owner has been identified once at the time of account opening and no change in the ownership has occurred since

When the customer or the owner of the controlling interest is an entity listed on a stock exchange in India, an entity resident in jurisdictions notified by the Central Government and listed on stock exchanges in such jurisdictions, or a subsidiary of such listed entities
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 34(a)
source_excerpt: Where the customer or the owner of the controlling interest is (i) an entity listed on a stock exchange in India, or (ii) it is an entity resident in jurisdictions notified by the Central Government and listed on stock exchanges in such jurisdictions, or (iii) it is a subsidiary of such listed entities; it is not necessary to identify and verify the identity of any shareholder or beneficial owner of such entities.

question: What periodicity does the Direction prescribe for the system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts?
options: At least once in every two years
At least once in every twelve months
At least once in every three years
At least once in six months
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 37(a)
source_excerpt: A system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts, with such periodicity being at least once in six months, and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures shall be put in place.

question: Which transaction pattern does paragraph 36 say shall necessarily be monitored by the RE?
options: Routine salary credits made by an employer into the accounts of its employees
Withdrawals of small amounts made by customers categorised as low risk
Deposit of third-party cheques, drafts, etc. in the existing and newly opened accounts followed by cash withdrawals for large amounts
Balance enquiries and mini-statement requests made through internet banking or ATMs by customers categorised as high risk under paragraph 12
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 36(d)
source_excerpt: Deposit of third-party cheques, drafts, etc. in the existing and newly opened accounts followed by cash withdrawals for large amounts.

question: How frequently must periodic updation of KYC be carried out for a high-risk customer?
options: At least once in every two years from the date of account opening or the last KYC updation
At least once in every eight years from the date of account opening or the last KYC updation
At least once in every ten years from the date of account opening or the last KYC updation
At least once in every six months from the date of account opening or the last KYC updation
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 38
source_excerpt: periodic updation shall be carried out at least once in every two years for high- risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every ten years for low -risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

question: What is the prescribed periodic updation interval for a low-risk customer under paragraph 38?
options: Once in every ten years from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation
Once in every eight years from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation of the customer
Once in every two years from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation
Once in every five years from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 38
source_excerpt: once in every ten years for low -risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation

question: When only the address details of an individual customer change, how must the newly declared address be verified?
options: Through positive confirmation within seven days of the customer's self-declaration
Through positive confirmation within one year of the customer's self-declaration of the new address
Only at the next periodic updation of KYC, without any separate verification
Through positive confirmation within two months by means such as an address verification letter or contact point verification
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 38(a)(ii)
source_excerpt: the declared address shall be verified through positive confirmation within two months, by means such as address verification letter, contact point verificati on, deliverables, etc.

question: Under paragraph 41, whose approval must an RE obtain before opening an account for a Politically Exposed Person?
options: The Reserve Bank of India, before the account is opened in every case
Senior management
The board of directors of the RE at its next scheduled meeting
The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND) in advance of the account opening
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 41
source_excerpt: the approval to open an account for a PEP shall be obtained from the senior management

question: How must accounts opened through non-face-to-face onboarding under paragraph 40 be treated by the RE?
options: As low-risk accounts with periodic updation required only once in every ten years
As high-risk accounts subjected to enhanced monitoring until the identity is verified face-to-face or through V-CIP
As normal-risk accounts once the first transaction has been completed successfully
As accounts to be closed automatically if the identity of the customer is not verified within thirty days of opening the account
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 40(f)
source_excerpt: Such customers shall be categorized as high- risk customers and accounts opened in non-face to face mode shall be subjected to enhanced monitoring until the identity of the customer is verified in face-to-face manner or through V-CIP.

question: Under the simplified norms for Self Help Groups in paragraph 43, whose customer due diligence is needed to open the SHG's savings bank account?
options: CDD of every member of the SHG must be obtained at the time the account is opened
CDD of all the office bearers of the SHG shall suffice
CDD of the secretary and treasurer of the SHG only must be obtained
No CDD is needed, since SHGs are wholly excluded from these Directions
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 43
source_excerpt: CDD of all the members of SHG shall not be required while opening the savings bank account of the SHG. (b) CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

question: Under paragraph 46(a), from which date does the five-year retention period for records of transactions between the RE and the customer run?
options: the date the account was opened
the date of transaction
the date the business relationship ended
the date of the last KYC updation
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 46(a)
source_excerpt: (a) maintain all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction;

question: According to paragraph 46(b), customer identification and address records obtained at account opening must be preserved for at least how long?
options: five years from the date on which each transaction was conducted
five years after the business relationship is ended
three years after the account is closed
ten years from the date of opening the account
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 46(b)
source_excerpt: (b) preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship is ended;

question: Paragraph 46(e) lists the information that must be maintained so as to permit reconstruction of an individual transaction. Which of these is not on that list?
options: the nature of the transactions
the date on which the transaction was conducted
the parties to the transaction
the place where the transaction was conducted
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 46(e)
source_excerpt: (e) maintain all necessary information in respect of transactions prescribed under PML Rule 3 so as to permit reconstruction of individual transaction, including the following: (i) the nature of the transactions; (ii) the amount of the transaction and the currency in which it was denominated; (iii) the date on which the transaction was conducted; and (iv) the parties to the transaction.

question: According to Annex I, which mobile number must not be used to obtain the customer's signature on the Customer Application Form?
options: the mobile number of the authorized officer registered with the RE
the customer's own mobile number sent with the verification OTP
the mobile number of a family member clearly mentioned in the CAF
the mobile number of a known person recorded in the CAF
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), Annex I
source_excerpt: In any case, the mobile number of authorized officer registered with the RE shall not be used for customer signature. The RE must check that the mobile number used in customer signature shall not be the mobile number of the authorized officer.

question: For non-profit organisation customers whose details are registered on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog, what retention period applies under paragraph 46A?
options: five years from the date of upload on the DARPAN Portal
five years after the business relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later
three years after the registration on the DARPAN Portal
for the lifetime of the business relationship with no further period
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 46A
source_excerpt: REs shall also maintain such registration records for a period of five years after the business relationship between the customer and the RE has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.

question: Under paragraph 47, to whom shall REs furnish the information referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005?
options: the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit- India
the Chief Executive of NITI Aayog
the Ministry of Home Affairs acting as the nodal ministry
the Central Board of Direct Taxes that frames the reporting rules
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 47
source_excerpt: REs shall furnish to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit- India (FIU-IND), information referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 in terms of rule 7 thereof.

question: What does paragraph 49 permit an RE to do with account operations once a Suspicious Transaction Report has been filed?
options: freeze operations in the account for ninety days from the date of filing
impose no restriction merely on the basis of the STR filed
allow operations only with the prior approval of the Director, FIU-IND
restrict operations until FIU-IND acknowledges receipt of the STR
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 49
source_excerpt: REs shall not put any restriction on operations in the accounts merely on the basis of the STR filed.

question: Under paragraph 49, how is each day of delay beyond the time limit specified in the Rule treated when furnishing information to the Director, FIU-IND?
options: a single violation covering the entire period of delay
a technical lapse with no consequences under the Rule
a violation reportable only to the statutory auditor
a separate violation
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 49
source_excerpt: While furnishing information to the Director, FIU -IND, delay of each day in not reporting a transaction or delay of each day in rectifying a mis-represented transaction beyond the time limit as specified in the Rule shall be constituted as a separate violation.

question: According to paragraph 49, the confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit the sharing of what?
options: information under paragraph 4(b) of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual
the fact that records are maintained under rule 3 of the PML Rules
customer information for the purpose of cross selling with third parties
the complete transaction details to the Ministry of Home Affairs under the UAPA notification dated February 2, 2021
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 49
source_excerpt: However, such confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit sharing of information under paragraph 4(b) of this Master Direction of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual, if any such analysis has been done.

question: Under paragraph 48, what arrangement is required of the Principal Officers of REs whose branches are not all fully computerized?
options: fully computerize all its branches within one financial year at its own cost
have a suitable arrangement to cull out transaction details and feed them into an electronic file
furnish to FIU-IND every month the transaction details extracted manually from branches that are not computerized
report to the Reserve Bank the number of branches that are not computerized
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 48
source_excerpt: The Principal Officers of those REs, whose all branches are not fully computerized, shall have suitable arrangement to cull out the transaction details from branches which are not yet computerized and to feed the data into an electronic file with the help of the editable electronic utilities of CTR/STR as have been made available by FIU -IND on its web site

question: As per paragraph 51(a), how often must REs verify the UNSC Sanctions Lists and the lists in the Schedules to the Order of 2007?
options: on daily basis
once in a week
on the first day of every month
once every quarter
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 51(a)
source_excerpt: The aforementioned lists, i.e., UNSC Sanctions Lists and lists as available in the Schedules to the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as amended from time to time, shall be verified on daily basis and any modifications to the lists in terms of additions, deletions or other changes shall be taken into account by the REs for meticulous compliance.

question: Which Security Council resolution is cited in paragraph 51(a) as establishing the Taliban Sanctions List?
options: resolution 1267/1989/2253
resolution 1718
resolution 1988 (2011)
resolution 1540
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 51(a)
source_excerpt: ii. The “Taliban Sanctions List”, established and maintained pursuant to Security Council resolution 1988 (2011)

question: Under paragraph 51(b), how must details of accounts resembling individuals or entities in the sanctions lists be handled?
options: reported only to the Reserve Bank's concerned regional office, with no intimation to FIU-IND
advised only to the Ministry of Home Affairs, without reporting to FIU-IND
reported to FIU-IND with no intimation to any other authority
reported to FIU-IND apart from advising the Ministry of Home Affairs
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 51(b)
source_excerpt: Details of accounts resembling any of the individuals/entities in the lists shall be reported to FIU -IND apart from advising Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)

question: Under the Order referred to in paragraph 52, who has been designated as the Central Nodal Officer for the purposes of section 12A of the WMD Act, 2005?
options: the Joint Secretary (CTCR), Ministry of Home Affairs
the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
the Secretary, Department of Financial Services
the Director, FIU-India
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 52
source_excerpt: It may be noted that in terms of Paragraph 1 of the Order, Director, FIU -India has been designated as the CNO.

question: Under paragraph 52(h), within what period must an RE forward an application regarding unfreezing of funds to the Central Nodal Officer?
options: on the same day the application is received
within two working days
within ten days of receipt
within seven working days
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 52(h)
source_excerpt: Accordingly, copy of application received from an individual/entity regarding unfreezing shall be forwarded by RE along with full details of the asset frozen, as given by the applicant, to the CNO by email, FAX and by post, within two working days.

question: According to paragraph 53, with which order must REs ensure compliance, as amended from time to time by the Central Government?
options: the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007
the Order dated February 2, 2021 issued under section 51A of the UAPA
the Implementation of Security Council Resolution on Democratic People's Republic of Korea Order, 2017
the Order dated September 1, 2023 issued by the Ministry of Finance
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 53
source_excerpt: and also ensure compliance with the ‘Implementation of Security Council Resolution on Democratic People’s Republic of Korea Order, 2017’, as amended from time to time by the Central Government.

question: Under paragraph 54(c), what must be done with the written findings and documents examined on transactions with persons from FATF-flagged jurisdictions?
options: forwarded to the Director, FIU-IND, within thirty days of the examination
retained and made available to Reserve Bank/other relevant authorities, on request
submitted every quarter to the Central Nodal Officer designated under the WMD Act, 2005
destroyed after three years unless a suspicion arises later
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 54(c)
source_excerpt: The background and purpose of transactions with persons (including legal persons and other financial institutions) from jurisdictions included in FATF Statements and countries that do not or insufficiently apply the FATF Recommendations shall be examined, and written findings together with all documents shall be retained and shall be made available to Reserve Bank/other relevant authorities, on request.

question: What must REs apply to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons from countries for which the FATF calls for it, per paragraph 54(a)?
options: simplified due diligence measures with reduced documentation requirements
enhanced due diligence measures effective and proportionate to the risks
a complete prohibition on entering into or continuing any business relationship whatsoever
ordinary due diligence with no additional safeguards
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 54(a)
source_excerpt: apply enhanced due diligence measures, which are effective and proportionate to the risks, to business relationships and transactions with natural and legal persons (including financial institutions) from countries for which this is called for by the FATF.

question: According to paragraph 55(b), may details of information collected from customers for opening an account be divulged for cross selling?
options: No, not without the express permission of the customer
Yes, if the customer is informed after the disclosure
Yes, provided the information is at least two years old
No, unless the Reserve Bank grants written approval
source: Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Direction, 2016, DBR.AML.BC.No.81/14.01.001/2015-16 (Updated as on August 14, 2025), paragraph 55(b)
